summary: Built a read-only Zotero PDF resolver, swept all 52 no_source_pdf entries, gated non-key-anchored matches on year/similarity, and applied idempotently. Recovered 7 of 52 PDFs into sources/<doc_id>/, updated index.json (zotero_key/zotero_path), and re-ran the #835 fidelity audit (no_source_pdf 52->45). 1 needs human disambiguation, 2 confirmed false positives, 42 confirmed absent from this Zotero library. pdfs/ was never recreated.

artifacts.summary: Full 52-entry disposition table (7 recovered, 1 html-only, 1 needs-disambiguation, 43 absent-from-zotero including 2 rejected false positives), decisions, plan deviations, and verification evidence.

decisions_made: index.json's pre-existing zotero_key field is a Better-BibTeX citekey, not a real Zotero API item key; resolver still title/author-searches but tiers by the field's presence rather than using it as a literal API path.

Added a 0.4 title-similarity floor and progressive title right-truncation to the resolver after an initial sweep produced 9 false-positive search-candidates in the arXiv cluster via common-surname collisions; all 30 arXiv-cluster entries now correctly resolve absent.
fine_2014_truthmaker-semantics-intuitionistic left as needs-confirmation per explicit plan instruction (year/title mismatch against best Zotero hit) -- not auto-accepted.

pnueli_1977 and een_2011 routed to decision: rejected (not needs-confirmation) since evidence is dispositive (wrong author / wrong domain), reserving needs-confirmation for the genuinely ambiguous fine_2014 case.
Literature repo commit staged index.json only -- the 7 recovered PDFs are excluded by that repo's own *.pdf .gitignore rule, matching its existing convention of not tracking binary PDFs.
dead_ends: Using index.json's literal zotero_key field value as a direct Zotero API item-key path segment (GET /items/<key>/children) -- 404s, the field is a citekey not a real key.
Full-title-only search query with no truncation -- silently returns zero hits when the corpus title carries a trailing descriptor word not in the real bibliographic title.

Taking the first search candidate with any PDF attachment as the match -- picks wrong papers when an unrelated item with a PDF outranks the correct HTML-only item in API result order (pnueli_1977 case).
